$comment: THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every status claim in this repo.
Nothing else may carry one. ROADMAP.md §0b/§0c and docs/completion-tracker.html are
GENERATED from this file by `node scripts/build-status.mjs` — edit here, never there, or the next
generate silently reverts you. RESUME.md is untouched by the generator: it answers a
different question (how something was proved, and what it cost to find out) and is
append-only archaeology.
status  — proved:   a human has seen it work on the phone
partial:  works, with a named gap
untested: code and tests are in, no human has ever exercised it
broken:   works badly, defect logged in ROADMAP §2
none:     not built
blockedBy — what stands between this row and being finished. This is the field that
keeps the brain dependency visible rather than buried in prose, and it is
why the generator can say 'the app alone cannot reach 100%' with a number
instead of an opinion.
brain:     needs jarvis-brain — a gateway route, a merge, or a deploy
desk:      needs the desk machine on
device:    needs the phone in hand, unlocked (adb cannot unlock it)
app-build: app repo, but needs a native build or an EAS credentials action
app:       app repo, ships over the air
none:      finished, nothing owed

otaVerified.note: Checked against the phone on every publish since 2026-08-24, when a publish went to a runtime no device had. Runtime is byte-identical to the fingerprint the installed APK carries, so a JS-only publish reaches the phone. A LOCAL build still receives nothing unless the fingerprint is baked by hand. Checked again on 2026-08-27, before the publish rather than after: `fingerprint:generate` returned the same 31c64113 the APK carries, and update 01a0422d went out to it. Twice on 2026-08-27, fingerprint checked before each: 01a0422d (the bell and the tab root), 01a04293 and 01a0429e (the chat order, in two halves) and 01a042b3 (the interrupted turn).

brain.label: Brain
brain.head: c86d176 on `fix/durable-state`; `feat/cloud-gateway` is what Render watches
brain.why: Closed deliberately, so the app can be worked without a second repo in the picture. Not a blocker that arrived — a decision that was taken. That repo is clean and fully pushed; nothing is waiting to go out of this laptop.
warnings: **This laptop cannot run gateway work at all, found 2026-08-28.** There is no Python on it — `python` and `python3` resolve to the Microsoft Store stub (`WindowsApps\python3.exe`) and `py` does not exist, so `pytest` cannot run, `cloud_gateway.py` cannot be imported, and a change to it could only be written blind. **The home machine is the only place any of this is testable.** Everything on this page is therefore a handoff and not a queue — the closing of `jarvis-brain` on 2026-08-26 was a decision, and as of today it is also a fact about the hardware.

**Two live gateway bugs were found on 2026-08-27 and deliberately NOT fixed here.** Both are in `jarvis-backend/cloud_gateway.py`, both are diagnosed down to the line, and both look like app defects from the phone. **(1) `_FAR_RE`, line 2757** — it accepts `to|from|until` before the destination, so *"how far is home from here"* extracts `dest="here"`, no route fact is added, and the model invents a distance with total confidence. Fix is not deleting `from` (*"how far from home to the office"* needs it): prefer a `to` destination when both appear, reject `here` / `my location` / `current location`, **and write a test per phrasing** — the entire defect is that one phrasing was never tried. **(2) the transcript at line 4095** — `await emit(...)` discards the bool, so when the socket has gone the spoken turn vanishes and only the answer survives, by push, leaving a reply with no question above it. `deliver()` at line 3977 is the pattern to copy; the push payload needs to carry the transcript so the app can write the user turn, because the code is right that a transcript sent as a status message lies about who spoke. **That second one is the only item on this page whose fix is not gateway-only:** the cause is entirely here, but `replyFromData` in the app (`src/lib/notify.ts`) returns `{text, at}` and nothing else, so a new field on the push would be dropped in silence. Land the two halves together, or the gateway change will look like it did nothing.

**A stored fact says where he is "currently", and it is what turned the regex bug into its worst answer.** The Memory screen carries `Kaustav is currently in Ichapur, West Bengal, India` — a time-sensitive claim living in a permanent store. With no route fact injected, the model reached for it, and with `Kaustav lives in Ichapur` beside it concluded *"you have already arrived at home"* — while the phone's own header read `Office`. **Fixing `_FAR_RE` alone does not fix this:** any lookup that fails quietly will reach the same stale fact, and the failure will look like confident knowledge rather than a gap. Either fact extraction refuses claims carrying `currently` / `right now` / `today`, or those facts expire; this one is redundant either way, since the `where` block carries live location on every single turn. Seen in the same list: `Kaustav asked about Marco Polo`, so extraction is also storing conversation trivia beside load-bearing records.

**Two of the rows below are already fixed and merely unshipped.** They are visible on the phone and will look like live app defects. Do not re-diagnose either from the app side — the fix is `c86d176`, sitting un-merged.

**Until `fix/durable-state` merges, every deploy silently disarms the briefing.** It has already happened twice, with nothing said anywhere. The merge is the whole of the deploy: `git merge fix/durable-state && git push` from `feat/cloud-gateway`.
The local checkout of `feat/cloud-gateway` is **42 commits behind its remote**. Work that feels missing from this machine is on GitHub. Fetch before concluding anything about that branch.
buildableAnyway: **Queue 11, the notification listener** — the spec and the pure drop-rule reducer, with tests, with no service registered and no permission asked. The gating on 12 is a privacy decision, not a sequencing one: a listener sees OTPs, balances and private messages, and once that is collected badly no later fix un-collects it.

**Queue 20's app half** — derive facts from turns, keep a ledger of what was sent, supersede what changed, send derived facts and never raw rows. `shareFacts` is the proved shape to copy. Consent rule comes first. Only the brain half is blocked: the ask envelope carries **one turn**, so he answers cold even though `chat_turns` holds the history.

Push, both channels and the departure briefing are proved, and since 2026-08-26 the phone fallback arms itself, reads the registration back and names its own refusals. What is missing is continuous presence: the notification listener, which is gated behind the token split — and four checks with the phone in hand, because surviving a reboot turned out to be nothing to build and everything to verify.

rows.name: Desk-key handshake (sealed turns)
rows.note: **Cause found and fixed 2026-08-29, unproved.** `has_desk_key: false` was read off the LIVE gateway with the desk off — which is the ordinary state of this system, since the PC being off is exactly why a fact is queued. The key was held in memory and in a file on Render's disk, so **every deploy and every free-tier spin-down returned the gateway to the one state where `queue_fact` cannot seal and drops the turn instead.** Eighteen went that way in a week. The desk's PUBLIC half and the sealed queue now mirror into the same Postgres `gateway_state` table the schedule uses, injected as a hook rather than imported so `fact_outbox` keeps its stdlib-only discipline; what crosses is ciphertext and one public key. `restore()` is additive, so it cannot race the container's own disk or drop a fact queued while the database was still answering. 44 checks in `test_fact_transport.py`, including a fixture that wipes memory AND disk the way a deploy does. **Owed: the deploy, the desk on once, and then `has_desk_key` still true after the deploy AFTER that.**

rows.name: `BRIDGE_SECRET` rotation
rows.note: **The blocker was ordering, and it is gone as of 2026-08-29; the rotation itself is still owed.** The gateway and the desk read this secret from two different places, so whichever moved first locked the other out — and the desk may be off when the change is made, which is why a known-leaked value stayed live for weeks. The gateway accepts `BRIDGE_SECRET_OLD` alongside `BRIDGE_SECRET` for one window now, logs loudly on every connect that still uses the old one, and reports `bridge_rotation: {old_accepted, connects_on_old}` on `/health` — so the old value can be deleted on evidence rather than on a guess. **His four steps are written out in `jarvis-backend/CLOUD_GATEWAY.md`:** set both and deploy, move the desk's `.env` when that machine is next on, watch the count reach zero, delete the old one. No window where either end cannot reach the other.

rows.name: Capability-split tokens
rows.note: **WRITTEN 2026-08-29 on the home machine, both halves, and NOT LIVE.** The gateway derives a short-lived token per capability from `APP_TOKEN` (`POST /app-tokens`, master-only): `link`, `push`, `state`, `memory`, `say`. A token is `j1.<cap>.<exp>.<mac>` with the mac keyed by the master itself, so verification is stateless, **rotating the master revokes every derived token at once**, and a leaked `push` token buys the push route and nothing else — it cannot even mint itself a new one. This app exchanges once and stores the set beside the master (`src/link/capabilityTokens.ts`), attaches the right one per route, and re-mints three days before they lapse. **The master still opens every route on purpose**: this install presents it, and an auth change that locked him out of his own assistant would be worse than the leak it prevents — `/health` counts every master use per route so the migration is a number. 68 checks in `test_app_tokens.py`, 20 + 3 + 7 jest here. **Owed: a deploy and an OTA publish, then `master_calls` going quiet.**

rows.name: Token expiry
rows.note: **Written 2026-08-29 with [token-split], and the same deploy is owed.** Every derived token carries an expiry (`APP_TOKEN_TTL_DAYS`, default 30, declared in `render.yaml`). An expired one is refused with `401 {"error": "token_expired"}` rather than a bare 401, because the difference decides what the phone does: this app mints again and retries **once**, and a second expiry after a fresh mint is a clock problem rather than something to loop on. A caller may ask for a shorter TTL and never a longer one. The master itself does not expire and is not meant to — it is the pairing secret in SecureStore, and rotating it is what revokes.

rows.name: Text chat, both directions
Replies arrive word by word
Markdown rendered, not shown as asterisks
The chat log in the right order, once each
rows.note:
**Proved on `84f40716`, 2026-08-27, on update `01a0429e`** — read top to bottom by scrolling the whole ~100-entry log, not from one screenshot, which is how this row was wrongly called done before. **Every timestamp ascends**, across four days and three day rules (`Friday`, `Tuesday`, `Yesterday`, `Today`), including the exact case reported broken: yesterday's 19:00 briefing sitting above today's 07:00.

It took two fixes today and the first was incomplete. `place()` orders what arrives; **`inOrder()` had to be added for what was already on disk**, because a relaunch restores the file as written and `place()` can never reach it — a fix that only guarded new entries would have left the phone looking identical and read as a third failure. That is `hydrate`'s own sentence about duplicates, applied to order.

**The one same-text pair in the log is not a duplicate:** two identical turns 60 seconds apart, and the operator confirms he sent it twice by hand after the first appeared to get no reply. Sixty seconds is far outside the 5-second window and the code is right to treat it as a second send. **What made him resend is a separate defect, recorded under `chat-stuck-sending`.**

rows.name: A turn interrupted mid-send stops claiming to be sending
rows.note:
**Found and closed on `84f40716`, 2026-08-27.** A `thanks Jarvis` from Monday 20:02 had been reading `SENDING` for three days: `sending` is the gap between `local_command` and `turn_sent`/`turn_failed`, both of which belong to a running process, so killing the app in between leaves the turn written to disk mid-flight with nothing to move it. Its owner read that as never sent and re-sent it by hand — **the only duplicate in that log is this bug's footprint.**

**Detected on restore, not by age.** A restored turn still saying `sending` has lost the process that owned the send, which is a fact; a threshold would be a guess about how long a send may take and would eventually accuse a slow one in the current session. Only the restored half is touched.

**A new state rather than reusing `failed`, and that distinction is the point.** `failed` renders `NOT SENT` and carries this app's one unambiguous retry, justified by nothing having carried the message. An interrupted turn may already have gone — the window spans `link.send()` — so `NOT SENT` would be a guess and a safe-looking `SEND AGAIN` on *run script X* could run it twice. `awaiting` asserts *carried*, equally unknown. `INTERRUPTED` says what happened and claims nothing about the outcome: tone `bad`, no retry, words left there to be copied.

**Seen on the phone at `01a042b3`:** the Monday turn now reads `You · 20:02 INTERRUPTED` in red. It repaired itself on load, since `hydrate` does the marking — no migration, and nothing else on the device had to change. 7 tests, 5 of which failed first.

rows.name: The voice rule applied to what the model writes
rows.note: **Found on the phone 2026-08-24.** `sir` is punctuation — lowercase, spent once. The situation line obeys it; every model reply capitalises it: *Standing by, Sir.*, *I can’t see your screen from here in the cloud, Sir.*, *I can’t authorise task approvals from the cloud, Sir.* Systematic rather than a one-off, and the same gap the nudge path has. The rule lives in `commute.ts` and `_briefing_text`; the persona prompt never got it.

rows.name: No unprompted weekday assertion
rows.note: **Seen again on the phone 2026-08-24, a Monday.** *I can’t authorise task approvals from the cloud, Sir. Are you working this Saturday, by the way?* — a weekend question appended to an unrelated refusal. Same class as the false Saturday shift: a stored Mon–Fri pattern being asserted as a fact about today. The fix is committed in the brain as `c86d176` and undeployed, which is exactly what this looks like.

rows.note: `_strip_reasoning()`. **Device pass 2026-08-24:** two full screens of real model replies read off the phone, including multi-sentence answers and one that reasoned about a screenshot — no monologue, no stray tags, nothing leaked. Previously proved in the harness only.

rows.note: On-device, no model, no await. **Read again 2026-08-24:** *12:24 PM, sir. You are at Office and Office briefing at 7:00 PM.* Note the lowercase `sir` — this line obeys the voice rule, which is what makes the replies below it violating the same rule so visible.

rows.name: A status panel naming every seam
rows.note: Eight rows, four states, assembled on the device so it is readable with nothing connected at all — which is exactly when it will be looked at. **Read on the phone again 2026-08-24, on the new bundle:** all eight rows render, the caption counts `1 OFF` for the sleeping desk alone, and the briefing row reads `AT THE GATEWAY` while the link is cloud. Named gap: the third briefing state added that day, `CANNOT TELL`, cannot be reached on a cloud-linked phone — the stamp is fresh, so it would take two days of workspace-only sessions or a debug build to see it. **Reviewed 2026-08-27 and the gap is not work — it is a state that cannot be induced.** `CANNOT TELL` needs `cloudArmedState` to read `stale`, which needs the upload stamp older than `CLOUD_TTL_HOURS` (48) or dated in the future. Neither is reachable on demand: the stamp refreshes on every cloud connect, and the only lever that would fake it is moving the phone's clock — **which must not be done**, because `timeline` is three days into a four-day count and the journal is time-keyed, so a clock move would cost more than this row is worth. It is covered by test (`statusPanel.test.tsx:73`), and the eight rows and four states have been read on the device twice. **This is the same shape as `fallback-armed` and should be left `partial` for the same reason** rather than being quietly promoted or treated as an open task: the honest `partial`s here are ones nobody can close, not ones nobody has done.

rows.name: Microphone in
rows.note:
**Run at last on 2026-08-27, and the transport passed on the first try.** `brains.usage.audio` went `{gemini_ok: 0, fell_back: 0}` to `{gemini_ok: 1, fell_back: 0, last_error: null}` — the clip reached the gateway, Gemini accepted it, and nothing fell back to Groq. **The mime fear this row was written around was already answered in code:** `_AUDIO_MIME` maps `m4a` to `audio/aac`, which is exactly what Google documents, so there was never anything to fix. Note the counter is incremented on a call that did not throw, so it proves the format was accepted and not that words came back — the chat is what settles that.

**The named gap is the transcript.** *"hi jarvis"* came back as **"ki service"**, and the reply — correct Benglish for the question it thought it had been asked, about what the cloud can do without the desk — was right for a transcript that was wrong. The cause is visible in `_GEMINI_TRANSCRIBE_PROMPT`, which primes hard for romanised Bengali (*"the speaker mixes Bengali and English… anything that sounds like Hindi is Bengali"*). That prompt exists to fix the opposite failure and it works; on a two-word English greeting it overcorrects, and `ki` is a real Bengali word. **One sample, and a poor one** — two words, one of them a proper noun the prompt never names. Cheapest thing to try is telling the prompt the assistant is called J.A.R.V.I.S., which is a gateway change and so blocked with the rest.

**2026-08-27, second clip: voice is cleared of the wrong answer it appeared to give.** A spoken *"how far is home from here"* was answered with an invented distance, which looked like the transcript being mangled again. **Typing the identical question reproduced it exactly** — so the fault is `_FAR_RE`, recorded under `weather-distance`, and had nothing to do with the microphone. `gemini_ok` reached 2 with `fell_back` still 0. **A separate defect did show up on that clip, and it is now diagnosed:** the transcript never rendered as a user turn, where the first clip's did. **The socket died while Gemini was transcribing, and only the answer has a lifeboat.** `emit()` returns False when the socket is gone; `deliver()` checks that and pushes the answer instead (`cloud_gateway.py:3977`), while the transcript at `:4095` throws the result away and has no push path at all. Confirmed on the device: `numPostedByApp` went 2 to 3, so the reply arrived by push — which is why the chat shows an answer with no question above it. The window is the app being backgrounded mid-turn, where `LinkMachine.suspend` closes the socket deliberately; the first clip survived it by being short. **The codebase already learned this and half-applied it** — `emit`'s own docstring says False was once indistinguishable from success, *"which is how a finished answer came to vanish silently"*. The transcript was never given the same protection. Fixing it wants the push payload to carry the transcript so the app can write the user turn: prepending it to the answer is not open, since the code is explicit that a transcript sent as a status message is a lie about who spoke.

rows.note: The largest single gap in the chat, and app-only — `expo-speech`. **Voice IN is no longer the unknown half, as of 2026-08-27:** the microphone path works end to end and only the transcript is unreliable. This row is unchanged — nothing speaks yet.

rows.name: The phone fallback is actually armed, and says so when it is not
rows.note: **Found unarmed on 2026-08-26, fixed, and the armed half proved on the device the same day.** `setCommuteTask` reads the registration back after asking, because `registerTaskAsync` resolving proves only that it did not throw; the result carries the platform’s words, every attempt is recorded for a screen to read after a relaunch, and `App.tsx` logs a failure rather than discarding it. **Proved:** WorkManager holds job `#u0a495/288`, the task executes and writes its stamp, and Places reports it truthfully. **The named gap is the other half — “says so when it is not”.** The phone re-arms itself at launch and on every visit to Places, so the unarmed state cannot be induced on demand; it is covered by tests and by the reading that named it, not by a sighting. **2026-08-27 did not move this and is worth recording as such.** The 07:00 window was the first real one with the phone armed underneath a live gateway, and the phone correctly stayed silent — so the fallback still has not been seen to POST anything. Standing down is the gate’s proof, not this row’s.

rows.name: Briefing content, thresholds, quiet-day announcement
rows.note: Thresholds on real figures, never the model. Quiet day announced with its figures rather than silently, after silence was read as breakage for four days. **The wording rotates as of 2026-08-26** — a persisted cursor per slot in `briefingVoice.ts` spends a pool of 6–7 remarks before any line returns, and the titles rotate with it. The figures deliberately do NOT vary: a measurement rephrased for novelty is one you can no longer compare with yesterday. Every variant keeps the actionable word, so Android truncating the shade cannot eat the instruction. 30 tests, and the rules are asserted over the whole table rather than over one rendering. **Only the phone-sent briefing is affected;** when the gateway is armed it writes its own text.

rows.name: Rotating wording in the gateway-sent briefing
rows.note: The phone rotates its own wording; the gateway does not. When `cloudArmed` is true the phone stays silent by design and the gateway posts `_briefing_text`, which is a fixed template — so on a cloud-linked phone the repetition the rotation was built to fix is still what arrives. Same shape as `briefingVoice.ts`: a pool per slot and a cursor that survives a deploy, which is why it wants `fix/durable-state` merged first rather than a second store that a redeploy wipes. **Seen rather than reasoned about, 2026-08-27.** The Office briefing at 17:59 on the 26th and the Home briefing at 07:00 on the 27th carry the identical remark — *"An umbrella, unless you’ve grown fond of arriving wet."* — and differ only in their figures, 51% against 65% with a storm line added. Two mornings, one sentence. It also cost a diagnosis: the changed figures read as rotated wording from the phone, and the gateway was briefly suspected of having gone silent.

rows.name: He speaks first, once a day
rows.note: Fired for the first time and was wrong: a bare substring match let a Mon–Fri pattern assert a Saturday shift, and the prompt then asserted it as true today. Fixed in the brain as c86d176, not deployed. The same body also capitalised `Sir`, which the voice rule forbids.

rows.name: Briefings visible in the Activity panel
rows.note: They had been filtered out entirely.

rows.name: Read / unread per entry, surviving a restart
rows.note: **Proved, and then found half-wired on 2026-08-27.** Marks are per entry and survive a restart. What they did NOT survive was reading the chat: there are two unread systems — `readAt`, the timestamp behind Home’s *"N new replies"*, and `readIds`, the persisted set behind the bell — and only the Activity panel ever wrote to the second. So reading the conversation cleared its own marker and left the bell counting the very turns it had shown. Fixed at `28d682d`, published as `01a0422d`, **and confirmed gone on the phone the same afternoon.** The same fix closes the case one step earlier: a reply landing while the chat is open is marked read as it arrives, where before the tab bar counted an answer being read on screen.

rows.name: The local task gated so it cannot double-post
rows.note: **Proved on `84f40716`, 2026-08-26 at 18:31:15.** A run forced inside the phone own departure window (18:30–19:00 for a 19:00 departure) while Home read `AT THE GATEWAY`: it exited in 260ms without fetching a forecast and posted nothing. The shade held exactly one briefing all evening — the gateway push at 17:59:18 — where 2026-08-21 saw both senders fire and the same briefing arrive twice. Forced rather than waited for, which settles the gate decision and not the scheduling; scheduling is proved separately by the unattended run at 18:07. **Held in a REAL window on 2026-08-27.** The 07:00 Home departure, with the phone rebooted the night before and the app never opened: exactly one notification arrived, and it was the gateway's. That is the same decision the 18:31 run settled by force, taken this time by a headless run nobody was watching.

rows.name: Full message on tap, day rules, paged list
rows.note: **Proved on `84f40716`, 2026-08-27**, on a timeline finally long enough to exercise every part of the row at once. The full message on tap: the 07:00 briefing whole, in a box that no longer collapses to a line — the defect this row was left `partial` for. The `Yesterday` rule separating two days, which had never been seen. And the paging: `SEE n MORE` revealed twelve at a time (`PAGE = 12`, `ActivityScreen.tsx:27`), the count fell by twelve a tap, the last page held four, and the button then removed itself rather than sitting there offering nothing. `TESTING.md` 3.2, 3.9 and 3.10.

rows.name: Facts stored and recalled
rows.note:
14 facts known. Volunteered exactly once, wrongly. **Read on the device 2026-08-27, all 17, and the store is in better shape than that sentence suggests** — parents, brother, employer and its address, both dogs with sex and dates, the PIN code, the marriage year. A photo of a dog he had never sent before was answered *"That's Puku, Sir. He passed away on the fifth of August last year"*, which matches the stored `died on 5 August 2025` exactly, and the disambiguation is real work rather than luck: **two dogs are stored**, and *"who he **was**"* (past tense) plus *male* selects Puku over Kitty, who is female and alive.

**One row on that screen is a bug, and it caused today's worst answer.** `Kaustav is **currently** in Ichapur, West Bengal, India` — a time-sensitive claim in a permanent store. When `_FAR_RE` extracted `dest="here"` and injected no route fact, the model reached for that, and with `Kaustav lives in Ichapur` beside it produced *"since you're currently in Ichapur, sir, you've already arrived at home"* while the phone's own header read `Office`. **So that answer was not invented from weights — it was a stale fact filling a hole the regex left**, which is worse, because it will happen again wherever a live lookup fails quietly. Every other fact on the screen is durable; this one is a snapshot wearing a fact's clothes, and the `where` block already carries live location on every single turn, so it is redundant as well as harmful.

Also visible: `Kaustav asked about Marco Polo`, which is not a fact about him at all. Extraction is storing conversation trivia beside load-bearing records.

rows.name: Anything he learns from what you actually say
rows.note: **The largest gap in the memory story, and it was not in this ledger until 2026-08-24.** `shareFacts` derives from the journal rollup and named places only — four keys, all about the handset: `phone:screen-time`, `phone:pickups`, `phone:top-apps`, plus the places. **Nothing reads the conversation.** How he works, who matters to him, what he cares about: durable only if typed by hand into the Memory screen. So a chat scrolls past `CHAT_CAP` (100 entries, roughly a day at real pace) and nothing was taken from it. The raw turns survive brain-side in `chat_turns`, so this is not data loss — it is that no turn is ever promoted to a fact.

rows.name: A chat log that is not a one-day window
rows.note: `CHAT_CAP = 100` in `hudReducer.ts`, original and deliberate — a phone should not carry an unbounded log. Measured 2026-08-24: the whole persisted log spanned **Fri 20:03 to Sat 15:28**, so at real conversation pace 100 entries is about one day. Worth naming because the cap is silent: nothing tells you a turn is about to leave, and nothing is harvested before it does — see [facts-from-talking]. The brain keeps the turns; only the phone forgets.

rows.name: One assistant across desk, phone and chat
rows.note: App and chat share one history. A desk answering with its own brain bypasses it, so those turns never join the shared history.

rows.name: Rolling memory durable across restarts
rows.note: In Postgres, not RAM — the RAM claim was stale. Whether the shared-memory flag is actually on in Render's environment is unverified.

rows.name: Deploy-durable gateway state
rows.note: Committed on `fix/durable-state`, two commits ahead of the gateway branch, undeployed. Until it merges, every deploy silently disarms the briefing.

rows.name: Chat history sent with the ask
rows.note: The envelope carries one turn.

rows.name: Journal: usage source, rollup, fact sharing
rows.note: Derived facts only, never rows — the pattern every later sense copies.

rows.name: The journal’s denial path
rows.note: Reads “I cannot see your usage, sir — the permission is off.” Collected history stays visible under HELD ON THIS DEVICE, which is the honest distinction.

rows.name: Any background work running unattended
rows.note: **Proved on `84f40716`, 2026-08-26 at 18:07.** The task ran with the app backgrounded and the phone disconnected from adb — nobody started it, and the count on Places moved from 1 to 2 with the stamp reading `Nothing was due`. Getting there needed the throttling lifted first: standby bucket **40 (RARE)** to **5 (EXEMPTED)** and the app added to the device-idle whitelist, after which `WITHIN_QUOTA` went from unsatisfied to satisfied and only the 15-minute timer remained. That is what the Battery restrictions row asks a person to do in Settings. Before that, measured the same day: roughly one job window a day and `Network: blocked=REASON_APP_STANDBY`.

rows.name: The commute task body exercised by a test
rows.note: 10 tests, with the task callback captured at import and invoked against the real module. The gate cases were confirmed by removing the gate.

rows.name: Location timeline
rows.note: Sightings at named places, median last-seen per day, its own 28-day store. Silent for its first four days, by design. **Device pass 2026-08-24:** it is accumulating — the panel reads *Learning your hours at Office* and its countdown had moved from `4 MORE DAYS` to `3 MORE DAYS` since 08-21, which only happens if sightings are being recorded at a named place. Named gap: nothing it has learned has been *used* for anything yet, so its output is still unseen. **The named gap is addressed in code, 2026-08-27.** The app was spending four days learning an hour and then telling nobody: the figure surfaced in exactly one place, the anticipation remark, which fires ONLY when you are 45 minutes past it. So on every ordinary day it had learned something and kept it — failing the anticipation doctrine's own third test, *a figure you could disagree with rather than an adjective*. The WATCHING row now says the hour itself (`6:40 PM`) with a note naming the place and the days behind it, instead of `Office, ready`. `null` stays a real answer: enough days with no median still reads `ready` and invents no time. **Unproved until the fourth day lands** — the row reads `1 MORE DAY` tonight, so opening the app at Office tomorrow is what makes it speak. 4 tests.

rows.name: Call log, archive import
rows.note: Native build, and fatal for a store listing.

rows.name: Named places, location sharing, located answers
rows.note: **Proved on `84f40716`, 2026-08-27, from the Office**, which is the first time this row has been exercised since the fix that touched it. Three things at once. Location sharing on and the header naming `Office` — the label set by standing there, not a geocoder’s guess. *"how far to home"* answered **39.3 km by road, about 38 minutes** — so `home` resolved to the place he named, and the route was measured FROM where he was standing rather than from a district. *"is it raining here"* answered *"currently clear at the office, sir, with no rain falling"* plus a **95%** chance later — figures, and the place named. Asked from the Office deliberately: *"how far to the office"* would have answered zero and proved nothing. `TESTING.md` 7.1 and 7.2.

rows.name: Weather and distance from measured figures
rows.note: The search provider is unverified, and a silent search failure looks exactly like hallucination. Routing is a public server that knows the road graph and not the road, so durations are free-flowing and the context says so. **2026-08-27, from the Office:** both lookups answered with real figures — 39.3 km / 38 minutes by road, and a 95% precipitation chance against a clear sky now. So routing and forecast are reaching a server and returning measurements, which is the half that could be checked from the phone. `/health` reports `search: tavily`. **The named gap is unchanged:** that a TAVILY search answers is still unverified, and a silent search failure still looks exactly like a confident answer — the two lookups above are the route and forecast paths, not the search path. **BROKEN, found 2026-08-27, and it is one regex.** `_FAR_RE` (`cloud_gateway.py:2757`) accepts `to|from|until` before the destination, so *"how far is home **from here**"* extracts `dest="here"`. Nothing matches a known place called "here", geocoding it returns junk, and **no route fact reaches the model** — which then answers from its weights and stored facts. Seen twice within fifteen minutes: *"you're currently in Ichapur, sir, you've already arrived at home"*, then *"approximately 23 kilometers from the office to Ichapur — a local train from Bidhannagar Road should get you there in about 30 minutes"*, both invented, both confident. The same question phrased *"how far **to** home"* answered 39.3 km correctly at 12:41, which is why this survived: **the feature works on the phrasing the test script uses and fails on the phrasing a person uses.** This is the exact shape this row was already warning about for search — a silent lookup failure is indistinguishable from a confident answer. Gateway-side, so it waits with the rest.

rows.name: The situation sent to the persona
rows.note: Place, battery, link — one field. The highest character-per-line change available anywhere in the plan.

rows.name: Opening an app on the phone by name
rows.note: Confirmed twice over: by `topResumedActivity` and by the target app’s own launch event. Needed a native build.

rows.name: Governance: parked actions, approve and deny
rows.note: Desk actions only.

rows.name: Desk-watch countdown, silence locks
rows.note: The desk owns the clock; the phone’s countdown is a readout, never a decision timer. Do not move it.

rows.name: Scripts: list
Scripts: create, update, delete, run by id
rows.note: Which is why editing is disabled.

rows.name: Run history
rows.note: Reports currently invents “Last run: 2h ago” from a fixture.

rows.name: Presence — awake but idle
rows.note: Inferred from socket state today.

rows.name: Declared rules (“tell me if I haven’t…”)
rows.note: Spec written and awaiting review. Its presence half rests on a measurement that no longer holds.

rows.name: Anticipation v1 — noticed when you open the app
rows.note: Decided in code from the journal against its own baseline and the next departure. At most one a day, never the same subject twice running, silent by default. **Device pass 2026-08-24:** the WATCHING panel read `2 OF 3 READY`, and its counters had advanced since 08-21 — `4 MORE DAYS` to `3 MORE DAYS`, and Today from `SPOKEN` to `LISTENING`. The day gate and the baseline counters are therefore working across days, not merely rendering. It was confirmed speaking on 08-21; whether a given remark is *worth* making is a separate question from whether the machinery runs. **Widened on 2026-08-28, and the budget was widened first.** Three triggers became seven — the app that moved past its own usual (`appDeltas`), being somewhere well before the hour you are usually there, being absent from somewhere you usually are by now, and a typed departure that no longer matches the hour you are measurably gone by. The enabler was `spokenStore` keeping **a day per subject** rather than one subject: with one slot and one remembered subject, every added trigger made the app *less* likely to say the useful thing, because a dull observation spent the day exactly as fast as a sharp one. Daily cap unchanged, quiet hours unchanged, every remark still quotes its own figure and refuses to speak below its day floor. **Absence is matched to the same weekday**, which is the gateway nudge bug written down as a rule. **Unproved on the device:** the new triggers have never fired on the phone, and the arrival one cannot fire before 08:00 at all, since the quiet hours start there.

rows.name: Anticipation that finds you in your pocket
rows.note: Needs the gateway push or a foreground service — the phone measurably cannot do it alone.

rows.name: Anticipation from learned habit rather than a written rule
rows.note:
**Blocked by time, not by work, and the spec says so outright:** *"Two to four weeks of baseline before 'unusual' means anything, and the senses in §3.2 to notice with. No amount of code shortens the first."* (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-21-anticipation-design.md`.)

**Two things worth separating, checked 2026-08-27.** First, *more triggers* is not this row. `anticipate-v1` has three — place, screen time, pickups — and a fourth is buildable today, since `rollup.ts` already computes `usual.top` per-app baselines beside `today.top`. That would be a fourth **hand-written rule over measured figures**, which the spec explicitly calls *not the same thing as a machine that learns your habits*. Building it strengthens `anticipate-v1` and leaves this row exactly where it is.

Second, and not previously recorded: **the baseline this row waits on is currently biased.** Sightings happen only when the app is opened (`timeline.ts` says so), so weeks of it would be weeks of a sample taken whenever he happened to look at his phone. So this is downstream of `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` in queue 23 as well as of the calendar — waiting three more weeks on the present sampling would not produce the baseline this row means. **2026-08-28:** the seven triggers now shipping are all rule-shaped and none of them shortens this. What did change is that four of them are measured against a baseline the phone builds itself, so the biased-baseline problem below is now load-bearing for more than one row: every sighting still needs the app to be open, which is queue 23 and background location.

rows.name: 19 screens, full suite and clean typecheck
rows.note: The number written in a doc goes stale — trust the run, not the comment.

rows.name: Standalone release APK, no bundler attached
Haptics, and an animation switch that works
OTA updates
rows.note: **Verified 2026-08-24.** Channel Active, branch linked, runtime matching the installed APK, latest group is HEAD. A **local** build still receives nothing unless the fingerprint is baked by hand — `prebuild` writes the literal placeholder and nothing logs a word about it.

rows.name: Contrast checked against WCAG AA
rows.note: 4.78 over the floor and 4.68 over the navy crown, against a bar of 4.5.

rows.name: A theme choice that did nothing — removed
rows.note: Dark and System were identical. A setting that does nothing is worse than an absent one.

rows.name: arm64-only build
rows.note: A config plugin, registered — so `prebuild` cannot silently revert it, which is this project’s most expensive recurring bug class. Roughly 35 MB against 100.7 MB across four ABIs. **The old ledger listed this as owed; it is done.**

rows.name: Motion defaulted from the OS
rows.note: Implemented at `src/theme/appearance.tsx:89` and spied on in a test; a deliberate toggle outranks it permanently. **The old ledger called this untested for want of code; it has code and a test, and owes only a device pass.**

rows.name: Light theme
rows.note: Broken by design — “System” behaves identically to Dark. Decide or remove.

rows.name: Appearance surviving a launch
rows.note: In-memory only. Accent, glow and motion all reset. The ledger claimed this for days.

rows.name: Crash and error reporting
rows.note: **The JavaScript half is built, 2026-08-28, and has never run on the phone.** `src/lib/crashLog.ts` keeps a derived record — name, message, redacted frames, and which build it happened on — five deep in AsyncStorage. `ErrorBoundary` writes the render crash it already displayed, and `installCrashHandler` wraps the global handler for everything outside render, calling the one it replaced so the app still dies exactly as it would have. Settings → Diagnostics reads them back, copies a report, and carries a count of what has not been looked at. **Redaction has a test per rule**, because an error message quotes its own input: a parse failure on a gateway frame would otherwise carry that frame — token and chat text included — into the one store whose purpose is to be pasted into a chat window. **Unproved on the device, and shippable over the air** — the runtime is still `31c64113`, checked after the change. **The native half is unchanged and still owed:** a native crash takes the process with no JS involved, so nothing here sees it; that is a service and a build, and belongs to queue 23.

rows.name: A real release keystore
rows.note: Signed with Expo’s generated debug keystore, which is why a local APK and an EAS-signed one cannot replace each other.

rows.name: Screen-reader pass
rows.note: Targets are floored at 44–64px and roles are set; nothing has been checked with TalkBack.

rows.name: Tablet and landscape
rows.note: Locked to portrait. The reactor and the 2×2 grid need a breakpoint before a tablet is claimed.

timeline.title: The HUD, and the shape of the thing
timeline.detail: 19 screens, five tabs, the reactor. One reducer for the link so every tab agrees about what is connected.

timeline.title: Named places and located answers
timeline.detail: Coordinates resolved on the phone, because `KnownPlace` exists nowhere else. Unverified since the fix that touched it.

timeline.title: The journal, and derived facts only
timeline.detail: Usage read on the device, rolled up, and shared as a rollup rather than rows. The pattern every later sense copies — and the reason a notification listener is designable at all.

timeline.title: Every state must name itself
timeline.detail: It came up five times in one day. The briefing that never ran and the briefing that ran and found nothing to say were indistinguishable from outside, which let a wrong hypothesis stand for a day.

timeline.title: Background work: measured, not assumed
timeline.detail: `expo-background-task` hardcodes `setRequiredNetworkType(CONNECTED)`, and the uid reads `blocked=REASON_APP_BACKGROUND|REASON_APP_STANDBY` with `#netAvail=0` in a RARE bucket. **Stopped, not deferred.** Every presence decision since is chosen around this.

timeline.title: He speaks first — and gets it wrong
timeline.detail: The first unprompted remark asserted a Saturday shift on a Friday. A bare substring test matched a Mon–Fri work pattern, and the prompt then asserted it as true today. Fixed in the brain the same day; still undeployed.

timeline.title: The briefing arrives twice
timeline.detail: Naming Home armed both senders at once — the gateway push and the phone's own task, byte-identical strings so the shade could not tell them apart. The old plan said *keep the local task as a fallback*; it was never gated, so it was a second sender.

timeline.title: A local build silently breaks OTA
timeline.detail: `prebuild` writes the literal `file:fingerprint` into `strings.xml`; EAS substitutes the real hash and a local Gradle build does not. The APK then asks for updates matching a placeholder, gets none, and runs its embedded bundle forever. Nothing logs a word. Cost an hour.

timeline.title: The status panel, and anticipation v1
timeline.detail: Eight seams, four states, assembled on the device so it reads with nothing connected — which is exactly when it is looked at. Anticipation decides in code from the journal against its own baseline.

timeline.title: The OTA channel gate closed
timeline.detail: One command, read-only. Channel Active, branch linked, runtime byte-identical to the installed APK. The fear was an empty channel — the app asks and gets nothing, silently. It is not empty.

timeline.title: One source of truth for status
timeline.detail: Three files were carrying status claims and drifting. Now `docs/status/ledger.json` holds them all and everything else is generated, so a percentage cannot disagree with the row it came from.

timeline.title: The briefing row stops asserting what it cannot know
timeline.detail: A workspace-only week ages the upload stamp, and the panel read that as the gateway having lost the schedule. Three states now. The task's gate is untouched — a stale stamp still means the phone posts.

timeline.title: An npm script changes the runtime fingerprint
timeline.detail: `packageJson:scripts` is a fingerprint input. Adding two convenience scripts moved the runtime from `31c64113` to `3f9be979`, and the first OTA publish went to a runtime **no device has** — arriving nowhere, with a success message. Caught by reading the publish output against the installed fingerprint. The scripts were removed; the generator is invoked directly.

queue.title: Confirm the OTA channel
queue.detail: Was one command and gated every JS-only fix behind it. Channel `production` Active, branch linked, runtime byte-identical to the installed APK. **Proved end to end:** the publish that followed landed on the matching runtime, which is the only thing this check ever claimed.

queue.title: The briefing-schedule row stops lying
queue.detail: A workspace-only week ages the upload stamp, and the panel asserted the gateway lost the schedule — which the phone cannot know. Three states now: `AT THE GATEWAY`, `CANNOT TELL`, `ON THIS PHONE`. `cloudArmedState()` sits beside `cloudArmed()`, so the task gate is untouched and a stale stamp still means the phone posts. 10 tests; committed `d5eff11`; published to runtime `31c64113`. **On the phone 2026-08-24:** the new bundle is live (the update server serves it for this exact runtime and the app reports nothing newer), the panel renders, and the briefing row reads `AT THE GATEWAY` correctly while the link is cloud. **Still owed:** the new `CANNOT TELL` state itself is unreachable on a cloud-linked phone — the stamp is fresh — so it needs two days of workspace-only sessions or a debug build.

queue.title: The chat log in the right order, once each
queue.detail: **The ordering half is fixed; the duplicate half already was.** The note this item carried was stale — it asked for the real `at` values before more code, and `96de0e1` had already got them from a shipped audit and turned the exact-millisecond key into a 5-second window. What remained was that the chat rendered in ARRIVAL order: `ChatScreen` reversed the array without ever sorting by `at`, so a turn swept out of the tray carrying last night's stamp was appended last and read as the newest — yesterday's `15:xx` below today's `12:xx`, the second reported symptom. Fixed in the reducer rather than at the reader, because two readers assumed the array was ordered and `activity.ts` sorted the same data before showing it. 4 tests, 2 failed first; 999 tests green, `tsc` clean. **Closed 2026-08-27 on the phone**, on `01a0429e`, by scrolling the whole log rather than reading one screen — the previous fix here was called done from a screenshot and was not.

queue.title: Provider effects that outlive their tree
queue.detail: **Closed 2026-08-26.** An effect resolving after its test body corrupts the act environment, after which every later render returns an empty tree — no throw, no warning. It cost six tests. Fixed where `jarvisProvider.test.tsx` said it had to be: at the source, not inside each `.then`. `state/live.ts` is a per-run cancellation scope — a factory rather than a hook, because a provider-lifetime guard cannot cancel a dependency change and the alert registration at `[alert?.id, alert]` needs exactly that. All nine settle sites open one and end it from the effect cleanup; the one that hands a registration back on a dead run keeps its `l.alive` branch, named explicitly in a test so a second exception cannot appear quietly. The inventory is the argument for a primitive: eight sites carried a hand-written `let alive` and the ninth did not, and nothing could have told you which. 13 tests — 8 on the scope, 5 on the provider, including a source scan that fails if a bare settle reappears. Proved by mutation: reinstating the bare `.then` fails the scan, restoring it passes. No device needed, and none used.

queue.title: A crash says what it was
queue.detail: **The JS half is written and green as of 2026-08-28. Nothing has been published, and nothing has been seen on the phone.** A crash used to restart in silence, with `adb logcat` on the one machine that built the APK as the only diagnosis. Now: a derived record — no chat text, no token, because a crash log is exactly what gets pasted into a chat window — written by the boundary for a render crash and by a wrapped global handler for everything else, read back at Settings → Diagnostics with a count on the row for what has not been looked at. **What is left is a publish and a look at the phone.** A native crash still needs a service and a build, and stays owed rather than quietly folded in.

queue.title: He answers out loud
queue.detail: Voice out is the largest single gap in the chat, and app-only. The decision of whether and what to speak is pure and testable; the native call sits at the edge. Stop any utterance in flight before starting the next — two voices over each other is worse than none.

queue.title: He comes back after a reboot
queue.detail: **Closed 2026-08-27 on the device, and it cost no code at all.** The phone was rebooted on the night of 26 Aug with the run count on Places at **22**, and the app was not opened afterwards. A briefing arrived at 07:00, and the count read **28** when the app was first opened that morning — six runs nobody started, from a process that had been killed by a reboot. WorkManager rescheduled its own queue at boot, which is exactly the bar `TESTING.md` 1.9 sets. By 10:27 it read 37. The premise this item was written on had already been corrected on 2026-08-26: `dumpsys package` on the installed APK says `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED: granted=true`, `expo-task-manager` declares a receiver on `BOOT_COMPLETED`, and there was never anything to build here — only a check nobody had run. **The 07:00 run cannot be read after the fact:** the heartbeat keeps one outcome, not a history, so nine later runs have overwritten whatever that one recorded.

queue.title: Speak into the microphone
queue.detail: **Run on 2026-08-27 and no longer the oldest unverified thing here.** Held the mic, said *"hi jarvis"*, and `brains.usage.audio` moved from all zeros to `gemini_ok: 1` with no fallback and no error — so the audio reaches the gateway and Gemini accepts the m4a. The mime worry was unfounded: `_AUDIO_MIME` already maps `m4a` to `audio/aac`. **What is left is accuracy, not plumbing:** the transcript read *"ki service"*, and the reply was correct Benglish for that question rather than for the one asked. `_GEMINI_TRANSCRIBE_PROMPT` primes for romanised Bengali by design and overcorrects on plain English — a gateway change, so it waits with the rest of the brain work.

queue.title: The journal denial path, and the other never-run paths
queue.detail: Settings → Journal → usage access off → return. It must say *I cannot see your usage*, never *Nothing recorded*. Built, tested, and never once run by a human. Same sitting: the location timeline and anticipation v1, both unexercised for the same reason.

queue.title: Usable by someone who cannot see it well
queue.detail: Better than the old ledger admitted: contrast is measured at 4.78 and 4.68 against a 4.5 bar, and reduced motion already follows the OS with a test on it. What is genuinely owed is the label audit and a TalkBack pass.

queue.title: The photo half of the chat
queue.detail: A thumbnail instead of the word Photo — a reply about a photo cannot be judged without the photo — plus an in-flight indicator, and a failed send that stays recoverable with its caption. The longest wait in the app and the least visible.

queue.title: Appearance surviving a launch
queue.detail: In-memory only: accent, glow and motion all reset. The ledger claimed this for days, which is its own lesson. Cheap, ships over the air, and the kind of thing a person notices immediately.

queue.title: The notification listener
queue.detail: The step change in presence — event-driven, nearly free, and more context than any polling can buy. **Gated on the token split, which is gateway work:** a listener sees OTPs, balances and private messages, and once that is collected badly no later fix un-collects it. What can be built now is the spec and the pure drop-rule reducer, with no service registered and no permission asked.

queue.title: Split APP_TOKEN by capability
queue.detail: One string gates the socket, push, `/app-commute` and `/app-state` alike, and nothing expires. The gateway validates both halves, so it cannot land here. The gate in front of every new sense, not a follow-up.

queue.title: Merge fix/durable-state, then deploy
queue.detail: Until it merges into the gateway branch, **every deploy silently disarms the briefing** — which has already happened twice. Also carries the fix for the false Saturday shift, committed as `c86d176` and still not live.

queue.title: The situation sent to the persona
queue.detail: Place, battery, link — one field on the envelope. The most character per line of code available anywhere in the plan, and it is a gateway change.

queue.title: Delivered and read ticks
queue.detail: The phone knows *sent*. Only the gateway can say *delivered* and *read*, and it says neither. Needs a per-message id on both sides — and reply-to-a-message wants the same id, so it follows rather than inventing a second identity for a message.

queue.title: The desk-key handshake, and rotate BRIDGE_SECRET
queue.detail: 18 sealed turns dropped and rising, so the encrypted path has never once worked end to end. The old secret went through a log and still opens `/desk-link`. **The only item whose cost grows while deferred** — do both in one sitting rather than waiting for the desk twice.

queue.title: Run run_harnesses.py
queue.detail: Never executed by a Python interpreter with the real imports. This laptop has no Python — `python` opens the Microsoft Store. A duplicated-call SyntaxError already slipped through once and was caught by reading.

queue.title: A real release keystore
queue.detail: Release is signed with Expo's generated debug keystore, which is why a local APK and an EAS-signed one cannot replace each other. Fine for one phone, and the blocker on the second. **Folded into queue 23 on 2026-08-27** — it is free during a build that is happening anyway, and the spec sequences it with the other three.

queue.title: The Iron Man styling pass
queue.detail: Scope is styling: the logo does not change and no copy changes. The pieces exist and are under-used. Land it on one screen and live with it for a day before propagating — the item most likely to sprawl. The Android glass blur stays last of all: it adds no capability and its failure mode is a segfault that takes the process.

queue.title: Promote what he is told into what he knows
queue.detail: Today he learns four things, all about the phone: screen time, pickups, top apps, plus named places. He learns **nothing** from what you say — the only route from a sentence to a durable fact is typing it into the Memory screen yourself. Meanwhile the chat window holds about a day and rolls silently. The pattern to copy already exists and is proved: `shareFacts` derives, keeps a ledger of what it already sent, supersedes what changed, and — critically — sends **derived facts, never raw rows**. A turn-to-fact pass wants the same shape and the same restraint, plus a rule about consent, because quietly distilling everything a person says is a different product from one that remembers what it was told.

queue.title: A day boundary in the chat
queue.detail: The log renders times with no date, so Saturday noon reads as this morning — it misled a debugging session on 2026-08-24 before the timestamps were read directly. Small, and it is the difference between a log you can trust and one you have to decode.

queue.title: The gateway briefing repeats itself too
queue.detail: **WRITTEN on the home machine 2026-08-29 (`02604c6`) and NOT LIVE.** Ported from this repo's `src/lib/briefingVoice.ts` line for line rather than reinvented, because two senders with two voices is worse than the repetition: a pool per slot, one cursor object shared across departures, the figures never varied, and the actionable word (`umbrella`, `jacket`, `Water`, `hair`, `wait it out`) kept in every variant, since Android truncates a body in the shade. The cursor is spent only on a briefing that actually went out — `_push_all` returns whether anything left, and a push that reached nobody now leaves the day OPEN rather than marking it done, which is the rule the failed-forecast path already had. It persists through `_persist("briefing_voice")` and is restored on boot, the half that waited on durable state: a cursor a deploy resets restarts the rotation at the same line every time. `_briefing_text` without a cursor still draws the first line of every pool, so the prose the harness asserts is unchanged; `test_commute_briefing.py` 15 -> 26, negative-tested by committing the cursor before the push instead of after. **Owed: a deploy, then two mornings of looking at the notification.**

queue.title: The next native build — alarms, battery, background sightings, keystore
queue.detail:
**Specced 2026-08-27, awaiting approval: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-next-native-build-design.md`.** Prompted by *"can the app set alarms?"* — it cannot, and it says so honestly in the log. `AlarmClock.ACTION_SET_ALARM` would be perhaps forty lines, **and it cannot be published**: `android.permissions` is a fingerprint input, so one permission moves the runtime and a publish then reaches no device at all.

So the unit of work is the APK, not the feature, and **three other things have been waiting for one**: `expo-battery` for the missing half of §3.2.1, `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` for the `timeline` row's structural weakness (sightings only happen when the app is opened), and the real release keystore from queue 18, which is free during a build that is happening anyway. Spending a build on alarms alone and finding the next item a week later is the failure the spec exists to prevent.

**Background location is the one to argue separately** — it is the only item that changes what the app knows while closed. The alarm design is deliberately narrow: recognised on the phone rather than by the model (`asOpenAppCommand`'s rule, since a model asked to set an alarm can only say it did), ambiguity declines — *"set an alarm for 6:30"* is twice a day and asks — and `EXTRA_SKIP_UI` stays false so a human confirms what a regex parsed.

queue.title: The distance question answers with invented numbers
queue.detail: **One bug in two halves, and fixing either alone leaves the other able to produce the same confident wrong answer.** `_FAR_RE` (`jarvis-backend/cloud_gateway.py:2757`) accepts `to|from|until` before the destination, so *"how far is home from here"* extracts `dest="here"`, nothing matches a known place, no route fact is injected — and the model answers from its weights and stored facts, with a number and a train. It answers *"how far to home"* correctly, which is why every previous check passed: **the feature works on the phrasing the test script uses and fails on the phrasing a person uses.** The second half is the fact `Kaustav is currently in Ichapur` — a time-sensitive claim in a permanent store, which is what the model reached for when the gap opened, producing *"you have already arrived at home"* while the phone's own header read Office. **Fix:** prefer a `to` destination when both appear, reject `here` / `my location` / `current location`, **with a test per phrasing** — the whole defect is that one phrasing was never tried — and stop storing time-sensitive claims as permanent facts, which the `where` block already makes redundant. Found by typing, not by speaking: a voice answer looked like a transcription failure until the identical typed question reproduced it.

queue.title: A spoken turn that outlives its socket arrives with no question above it
queue.detail: **BOTH HALVES ARE WRITTEN, on the home machine, 2026-08-29 — and neither is live.** Gateway `2301ad7` on `feat/cloud-gateway`: the transcript `emit()` result is read rather than discarded, and when the socket died before it left, the text rides on the reply's push as `data.transcript`. App half in this repo: `replyFromData` reads that field for `kind: reply` only, `take()` dispatches a `transcript` frame above the answer with the same `at`, and the reducer deduplicates a user turn the way it already did a pushed reply — the tray sweep re-enters the same notification on every return to the foreground, which would otherwise have appended his question again under its own answer. **What is owed is a deploy and a publish, not code:** Render has to take the gateway commit and the app half has to go out over the air before anyone can see it. Then the device proof, which is the original repro — ask by voice, pocket the phone, and read what the chat shows when it comes back. Tests: `test_app_link.py` 42 -> 46 (three drive the real handler with `send_json` failing on exactly the frame a pocketed phone loses; one pins the discarded-`emit` statement form a refactor would restore), and 1119 jest across 80 suites here, typecheck clean.
